plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug exposure DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: Salmon gene-level counts from 3 treated vs 3 control zebrafish larvae pools (12000 genes x 6 samples, one batch) go through a standard DESeq2 workflow: sample-structure QC, minimal low-count pre-filtering, median-of-ratios normalization built into the DESeq2 negative-binomial fit, a Wald test on an explicit condition factor (treated vs control, control as reference), apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold changes, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control with independent filtering. Because zebrafish has no curated MSigDb/Hallmark gene set collection in the reference store, DE gene symbols are mapped to their one-to-one human orthologs (via org.Dr.eg.db and/or a babelgene ortholog table) before a preranked fgsea GSEA against the human MSigDB Hallmark and WikiPathways-human collections; the ortholog-mapping loss is reported explicitly. With only 3 replicates per group the design has low power to detect anything but large fold changes — this is stated up front and the significance threshold is not loosened to compensate. The final report consolidates DE results, diagnostic plots, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and the full reproducibility record.
